newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish mobile phone company eyes police masts.
newsitem.headline: Irish mobile phone company eyes police masts.

text.p: The Irish police have come to the rescue of a company setting up the country's second mobile telephone network -- it is discussing renting its radio masts.
The Justice Ministry said on Thursday that it was discussing renting a number of masts to ESAT Digifone, which is launching a mobile network to rival the state's Telecom Eireann network.
"Commercial terms have been agreed in principle," a spokeswoman for the ministry said.
She declined to say how many of the police force's radio masts were under discussion but industry sources said it involved hundreds of the installations.
Similar agreements have been concluded in Norway and in the U.S. city of Boston, industry analysts said.
Conclusion of the agreement is expected to give the company a major boost in its plans to launch a mobile network for the corporate sector by Christmas and to the public next year.
It will allow ESAT to fill in many "black holes" -- areas where its mobile phone signals are weak or non-existent because of the terrain or distance, the analysts said.
